g1-implement.title: Affordance, byte-faithful writer, and the two prose corrections: implement
g1-implement.imperative:
Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for this gate and dispatch a subagent invoking constellation-implementer. Three changes, one coherent bite: (1) scripts/checklist_engine.py -- let amend's `retext-check` op run on a SURVEY checklist as well as a gated one, keeping add/drop/rescope gated-only (a conservative choice, not a type-level impossibility -- say so in the refusal message). State in the reviewer-facing prose what amend's --authority and --reason mean for a survey retext: the authority is the dispatching Commander, named in the reviewer handoff, never a string the reviewer invents. (2) scripts/checklist_engine.py save() -- preserve the target file's EXISTING line ending and write bytes; a file that does not yet exist, or one with mixed endings, gets LF. Scope is save() only; the journal append near line 2762 is out of scope and raised as a triage candidate. (3) skills/reviewer/ -- rewrite r6-fowler's imperative to name BOTH paths: resolve the real record path when you INSTANTIATE the survey, before you claim (the normal path), and use `amend --op retext-check` to repair it if the record moves or the path was wrong (the repair path). Do not make the exceptional route read as the documented route. Also correct SKILL.md's 'an open fail cannot consolidate to APPROVE' to state the --override-reason path. The line-ending test MUST be observed red before green. Both fixtures ship and both earn their place: on Windows the LF fixture is the discriminating one for THIS bug (text-mode write_text already emits CRLF here), and the CRLF fixture is the guard against the obvious over-correction of always writing LF. Three test shapes that cannot fail, all forbidden: building the LF fixture with write_text (on Windows it is born CRLF and the discriminating test silently degenerates); asserting on read_text output (universal newlines make `
 not in read_text()` vacuously true); asserting the saved bytes equal the fixture's bytes (save re-serialises with indent=2, so it fails for the wrong reason and gets loosened). Assert on read_bytes, scoped to line-ending bytes. Name which fixture goes red on which platform. Wait for and integrate the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.

g1-review.title: Affordance, byte-faithful writer, and the two prose corrections: review
g1-review.imperative: Fill templates/REVIEWER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch a subagent invoking constellation-reviewer. Independently reproduce the red: the reviewer must itself observe the line-ending test failing against a text-mode writer, not accept the implementer's transcript. It must also confirm that lifting retext-check did not open add/drop/rescope on surveys, and that the rewritten r6-fowler imperative names a verb that actually works on a survey. It must inspect the returned survey's `amendments` audit array -- the safety argument for lifting retext-check rests on that trail, and a trail nothing reads is on paper. Name which fixture it observed red on which platform. Wait for and integrate the returned REVIEW_RESULT as evidence.
